SUBJECT:  ORDINANCE  2025-04-CC  AMENDING  TITLE  9 (BUILDINGS),  OF  THE
SOUTH  GATE  MUNICIPAL  CODE,  IN  ITS  ENTIRETY  BY  ADOPTING  BY
REFERENCE  THE  2025  EDITION  OF  THE  CALIFORNIA  CODES  OF
REGULATIONS,  TITLE  24 AND  THE  2024  EDITION  OF  THE  UNIFORM  SOLAR,
HYDRONICS  AND  GEOTHERMAL  AND  THE  2024 EDITION  OF SWIMMING  POOL,
SPA AND  HOT  TUB  CODES  PUBLISHED  BY THE  INTERNATIONAL  ASSOCIATION
OF PLUMBING  AND  MECHANICAL  OFFICIALS

PURPOSE:  To  adopt  new  State  Building  Codes  which  are  mandated  for  statewide
enforcement  on July 1, 2026.

 RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider  waiving  the reading  in full  and
adopting  Ordinance  No.  2026-04-CC  amending  certain  chapters  and  sections  of  Title  9
(Buildings)  of the  South  Gate  Municipal  Code  by adopting  by reference  the 2025  California
Codes  of Regulations,  Title  24 ("2025  Building  Standards  Code")  and the 2024  International
Association  of Plumbing  and Mechanical  Officials  Codes

FISCAL  IMPACT:  It  is estimated  that  the  cost  for  the  purchase  of  the  2025  California
Building  Standards  Code books  for the City  staff will  be $7,000.  This  amount  will  be expended
from  funds included  in the FY 2025-2206  Budget  (100-602-42-6305  and 100-602-42-6340).

The new State Building  Codes  have significant  changes  from  previous  editions  and will  require
training  of Building  and Safety  Division  staff,  design  professionals  and contractors  in coming
months.  Training  on the new  codes  is currently  available  through  a number  of professional
associations  including  the International  Code  Council  (ICC),  the Intemational  Association  of
Plumbing  and  Mechanical  Officials  (IAPMO),  the  International  Association  of  Electrical
Inspectors  (IAEI),  and the California  Building  Officials  (CALBO).

ANALYSIS:  In  accordance  with  state  law,  the  2025  edition  of  the  California  Building
Standards  Code has been adopted  by the State Building  Standards  Commission  and published  in
the California  Code of Regulations,  Title  24 ("2025  Building  Standards  Code").

  1

  151
 State law mandates  that California  jurisdictions  enforce  the 2025  California  Building  Standards
Code,  effective  July  1,  2026,  for  all  new  building  constructions  in  California.  While  the
California  Building  Standards  Cornrnission  adopts  building  code standards  to be used statewide,
City  Council  action  to adopt these codes at a local  level  is also part of the code adoption  process.
Adoption  of these  codes  by the City  allows  for the inclusion  of administrative  provisions  and
limited  amendments  to  the  state  codes.  State  law  permits  local  jurisdictions  to  make
modifications  to  the  state  codes  that  are reasonably  necessary  because  of  local  conditions
provided  the  City  makes  express  findings  that  the  changes  are needed  because  of  climatic,
geologic  or topographic  conditions.  The  proposed  Ordinance  contains  the  adoption  of these
codes  and administrative  provisions  for  the  enforcement  of the codes.  The  Ordinance  makes
findings  regarding  local  geographic,  climatic  and  topographic  conditions  that  make  the
amendments  to the state codes reasonably  necessary  for building  construction  in the City.

In accordance  with  state law, the 2024 edition  of the Uniform  Swimming  Pool,  Spa and Hot Tub
Code and the 2024  edition  of the Uniform  Solar,  Hydronics  and Geothermal  Code were adopted
by the State Building  Standards  and published  by the International  Association  of Plumbing  and
Mechanical  Officials.

Administrative  provisions  of  the  California  Building  Codes  are  adopted  and  include  past
amendments  carried  forward  as recornrnended  by the City's  Building  Official.  Such amendments
include  provisions  regarding  permits,  fees, inspections,  completion  of residential  remodeling  and
Board  of Appeals  proceedings.  The City  has not made  any amendments  to building,  residential,
plumbing  and electrical  codes  for  over  twelve  years.  The  sections  for  the numerical  for  the
proposed  ordinance  have  changed  to  match  the  format  of  the  2025  California  Code  of
Regulations;  the context  has not changed.  A Summary  of existing  amendments  carried  forward
are provided  as Attachment  B. Revisions  to the California  Building  Code were made to improve
procedures  with  building  permits  and inspections  as follows:
  *  Clarification  on the expiration  of building  permits  for new  struchires  from  180  days to
  365 days.
  *  Clarification  on  the  expiration  of  building  permits  issued  to  legalized  unpermitted
  structures  (60 days).
  *  Clarification  on concealed  work  done without  required  inspection.
  *  Clarification  on requirements  for the issuance  of a certificate  of occupancy.
  *  Clarification  on the release  of utilities.
  *  Clarification  on the process  for legalizing  unpermitted  structures.
  *  Clarification  on the process  for structures  wich  cannot  be legalized.

BACKGROUND:  The State's  Building  Standards  Codes  have been subject  to a series of major
transformations  since the 2001  International  Code  Council  (ICC)  model  codes  were  introduced.
The 2025  State Codes  utilize  the most  up to date code  documents  which  have  been developed
through  a national  code development  process.  These  construction  codes  include  the California
Administrative,  Building,  Residential,  Electrical,  Plumbing,  Mechanical,  Energy,  Historical
Building,  Existing  Building,  Reference  standards  and Green  Building  Standards  as well  as other
related  codes.

Adoption  of Ordinance  No.  2026-04-CC  incorporates  the 2025  Building  Standards  Codes  and
the 2024 International  Association  of Plumbing  and Mechanical  Officials  (IAPMO)  codes which
will  keep  the  City's  building  regulations  consistent  with  those  of  the  State.  They  provide

  2

  152
 minimum  standards  to safeguard  life  or limb,  health,  property  and public  welfare.  The proposed
Ordinance  is necessary  to keep us in compliance  with  State regulations  while  allowing  the City
to properly  address  special  local  conditions.

ENVIRONMENTAL  ASSESSMENT:  Enviroru'nental  review  is  not  required  under  the
California  Environmental  Quality  Act  (CEQA)  pursuant  to  CEQA  Guidelines  Sections
15060(c)(2)  (the  activity  will  not result  in a direct  or reasonable  foreseeable  indirect  physical
change  in the environment)  and 15060(c)(3)  (the activity  is not a project  as defined  in Section
15378),  Title  14, California  Code  of Regulations,  because  adoption  of the proposed  Ordinances
has no potential  for resulting  in a physical  change to the environment,  directly  or indirectly.

NOTICING  REQUIREMENTS:  A public  hearing  notice  was published  in South  Gate Press
on April  16, 2026.  Information  regarding  the adoption  of the 2025  California  Building  Code and
local  training  opportunities  are available  at the Community  Development/Building  and Safety
Division  Website.

The  new  2025  California  Code  of Regulations,  Title  24 is available  for  review  at California
Building  Standards  Commission  website:  www.dzs.ca.gov/BSC/Codes.  Bilingual  public
information  is currently  posted  in  the  Department  of Community  Development  containing
important  information  regarding  this upcoming  change  to construction  codes used in the State of
California  and their  effective  date. Requests  to review  the 2025 Edition  of the California  Code of
Regulations  are available  through  the City  Clerk's  Office.

 SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  A  ORIZING  THE  CITY  MANAGER  TO PROVIDE
 WRITTEN  NOTICE  OF INTENT  TO WITHDRAW  MEMBERSHIP  FROM  THE
 INDEPENDENT  CITIES  RISK  MANAGEMENT  AUTHORITY  (ICRMA)

 PURPOSE:  To  authorize  the  City  Manager  to  provide  written  Notice  of  Intent  to  Withdraw
 membership  from  the Independent  Cities  Risk Management  Authority  (ICRMA)

 RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The  City  Council  will  consider  adopting  a Resolution  which
provides  the  Independent  Cities  Risk  Management  Authority  (ICRMA)  notification  of  intent  to
 withdraw  from  the  insurance  pool,  herein  referred  to  as the  Joint  Powers  Authority  (JPA),  in
 accordance  with  the ICRMA  Bylaws,  Article  V.

 FISCAL  IMPACT:  None

 ANALYSIS:  The City  of South  Gate belongs  to a Joint  Powers  Authority  (JPA)  with  12 other  local
 cities  for  general  liability  and other  related  insurance  coverage.  The  City  is cornrnitted  to reducing
 costs  and  identifying  a provider  who  offers  competitive  pricing,  sufficient  coverage,  excellent
 customer  service  delivery,  and other  supplemental  benefits.  These benefits  include  but are not limited
to safety  training,  customized  reporting  and data tracking,  employee  development  training,  and risk
management  training/consulting.

 With  the rising  costs of liability  insurance  coverage,  the City  staff  would  like  to explore  potentially
viable  and cost-effective  alternatives  and, after the City  has finalized  its search,  conducted  its research,
 and reasonably  compared  these alternatives  to ICRMA,  it would  like  to preserve  the City's  flexibility
to remain  with  ICRMA  or choose  another  provider  effective  for the 2027/2028  Fiscal  Year.  The reason
why  this item  must  be considered  by City  Council  now  is the ICRMA  bylaws  state that if an agency
wishes  to withdraw  from  membership,  it must  do so at least one full  fiscal  year before  the City  may

 officially  withdraw.  That  is, if the City  were to wish  to move  to a different  provider  beginning  July 1,
2027,  it must provide  a Notice  of Withdraw  Resolution  no fater than June 30, 2026,  or prior  to the start
 of the 2026/27  Fiscal  Year.  By submitting  this Notice  of Withdraw  to ICRMA,  it will  provide  the City
with  that flexibility  to make  the best decision  moving  forward.  In the event the City  desires  to remain
with  ICRMA,  it must provide  a Revocation  of its intent  to withdraw  by December  1, 2026.

  183
 BACKGROUND:  The City of South Gate has been a member of the Independent Cities Risk
Management Authority  (ICRMA)  since 1986, and it participates in the Liability, Property, Auto
Physical Damage, Crime and Cyber Programs with 12 other member cities from the greater Los
Angeles and Orange County areas. City staff believe that the City should periodically  evaluate the
market to ensure that the rates we pay through the JPA are the most cost effective and provide
comprehensive insurance  coverage.

 SUBJECT:  AMENDMENT  N0.  1 TO  CONTRACT  N0.  2023-65-CC  WITH  PIPE  TEC,
 INC.  FOR  CLOSED-CIRCUIT  TELEVISION  (CCTV)  INSPECTION  SERVICES  OF
 THE  CITY'S  SANITARY  SEWER  SYSTEM

 PURPOSE:  To  request  City  Council  approval  to  exercise  a one-year  extension  option  to
 Contract  No.  2023-65-CC  with  Pipe Tec, Inc. for continued  CCTV  inspection  and maintenance
 services  of the City's  sanitary  sewer system.

 RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Amendment  No. 1 to Contract  No. 2023-65-CC  with  Pipe Tec, Inc. to
  exercise  a one-year  extension  for CCTV  inspection  services  of the City's  sanitary  sewer
  system,  for an amount  not to exceed  $147,000;  and
  b.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute  Amendment  No. 1 to Contract  No. 2023-65-CC  in a
  form  acceptable  to the City  Attorney.

 FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  Amendment  No.  1 to Contract
 No. 2023-65-CC  is in the amount  of $147,000  and will  be funded  with  Sewer Funds  budgeted  in
 the FY 2026/27  0perating  Budget.

 ANALYSIS:  On May  23, 2023,  the City  Council  approved  Contract  No. 2023-65-CC  with  Pipe
 Tec, Inc. to perform  closed-circuit  television  (CCTV)  inspection  services  of the City's  sanitary
 sewer system.  The agreement  has a three-year  term  and is scheduled  to expire  on May  22, 2026.

 The original  Request  for Proposals  included  the option  for up to two  (2) one-year  extensions,  at
 the  City's  discretion.  Staff  recommended  exercising  the  first  one-year  extension  to  ensure
 continuity  of services  while  maintaining  compliance  with  the  State  Water  Resources  Control
 Board  requirements  and the City's  Sanitary  Sewer Management  Plan (SSMP).

 Pipe  Tec,  Inc.  has  satisfactorily  performed  the  required  services,  including  routine  CCTV
 inspections,  emergency  response  services,  and maintenance  activities  such as cleaning,  debris
 removal,  and system  troubleshooting.  Their  performance  has been  timely,  responsive,  and in
 accordance  with  City  standards.

  1

  187
 Extending  the  agreement  will  allow  the  City  to  continue  progressing  toward  its  required
inspection  cycle  of the sanitary  sewer  system  without  interniption.  Additionally,  the extension
provides  operational  efficiency  and  cost  stability  while  staff  evaluates  fuhire  procurement
options.

BACKGROUND:  The  City's  sanitary  sewer  system  is a critical  public  infrastructure  system
consisting  of approximately  119 miles  of sewer  mains,  over  2,400  manholes,  and thousands  of
service  laterals  that  serve  residential,  commercial,  and  industrial  areas  throughout  the  City.
Proper  maintenance  and monitoring  of this  system  are essential  to ensure  reliable  wastewater
conveyance,  protect  public  health,  and prevent  sanitary  sewer overflows  (SSOs).

The State Water  Resources  Control  Board  requires  municipalities  to implement  and maintain  a
Sanitary  Sewer  Management  Plan  (SSMP),  which  establishes  regulatory  standards  for  the
operation,  maintenance,  and inspection  of sewer  systems.  A key component  of the SSMP  is the
routine  inspection  of  sewer  pipelines  using  closed-circuit  television  (CCTV)  technology  to
identify  structural  deficiencies,  blockages,  root  intrusion,  grease  buildup,  and other  conditions
that may lead to system  failures  if not addressed  proactively.

To meet these requirements,  the City  conducts  CCTV  inspections  on a systematic,  rotating  basis
to assess the condition  of its sewer  infrastructure  and prioritize  maintenance  and rehabilitation
efforts.  These  inspections  provide  critical  data  that  supports  capital  improvement  planning,
emergency  response,  and ongoing  maintenance  operations.

Due  to the specialized  nature  of CCTV  inspection  services,  including  the need  for  advanced
equipment  and trained  personnel,  the City  contracts  with  qualified  firms  to perform  this  work.

  SUBJECT:  AMERICANS  WITH  DISABILITIES  ACT  (ADA)  GRIEVANCE  AND
  PROCEDURES  POLICY  ADOPTION

  PURPOSE:  To adopt  an ADA  Grievance  Policy  and Procedure  as required  by the City's  ADA
  Self-Evaluation  and Transition  Plan.  The proposed  policy  complies  with  the adopted  plans  and
  meets the requirements  of Title  II of the ADA  Act.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The  City  Council  will  consider  adopting  the proposed  ADA
  Grievance  Policy  and Procedure  as necessary  to comply  with  the City's  ADA  Self-Evaluation  and
  Transition  Plan as well  as Federal  requirements.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no fiscal  impact.

  ANALYSIS:  The City  previously  adopted  an ADA  Self-Evaluation  and Transition  Plan, which
  requires  the formal  adoption  of an ADA  Grievance  Policy  and Procedure.  Title  II of the ADA  also
  requires  public  agencies  with  50 or more  employees  to designate  an ADA  Coordinator  and adopt
  a grievance  procedure  to ensure prompt  and equitable  resolution  of complaints.  Adoption  of the
  proposed  policy  satisfies  these requirements  and brings  the City  into  compliance  with  federal
  regulations  and its adopted  Transition  Plan.

  BACKGROUND:  The Americans  with  Disabilities  Act (ADA)  was enacted  on July 26, 1990,  to
  ensure equal access to civic  life for individuals  with  disabilities.  Title  II ofthe  ADA  requires  public
  entities  to evaluate  accessibility  and, where  necessary,  develop  a Transition  Plan.

  On May  26,  2020,  the  City  Council  adopted  an ADA  Transition  Plan  to comply  with  these
  requirements.  While  the plan  included  a sample  grievance  procedure,  it directed  that  a formal
  policy  be adopted  at a later date.

  The proposed  ADA  Grievance  Policy  establishes  a formal  process  for addressing  complaints.  It
  requires  individuals  to submit  a grievance  within  60 days of the alleged  violation  through  various
  methods  (mail,  email,  phone,  or in person).  The ADA  Coordinator  will  acknowledge  receipt  within
  15 days, gather  information,  and work  toward  resolution,  with  a written  response  provided  within
  60 days.

  210
 If the complainant  is not satisfied  with  the determination,  an appeal  may be filed  within  15 days.
Appeals  may be directed  to the City Manager,  who will  issue a final  determination  within  30 days,
or to an independent  Hearing  Officer  provided  by the Los Angeles  County  Bar Association,  who
will  conduct  a hearing  and issue a decision  within  20 days. The decision  rendered  through  either
process  is final.

The  City's  ADA  Coordinators,  as designated  in the Transition  Plan,  include  the Assistant  City
Manager/Director  of Public  Works,  Deputy  City  Engineer,  and Engineering  Technician.

  City  of South  Gate
  Grievance  Procedure  Under
  The  Americans  with  Disabilities  Act

This  Grievance  Procedure  is established  to meet  the requirements  of the Americans  with
Disabilities  Act of I 990 ("ADA").  It may be used  by anyone  who wishes  to file a complaint
alleging  discrimination  on the  basis  of disability  in the  provision  of services,  activities,
programs,  or benefits  by the City of South  Gate  (the "City").  The City's  Personnel  Policy
governs  employment-related  complaints  of disability  discrimination.

The ADA  complaint  submitted  pursuant  to this Grievance  Procedure  should  be in writing
and contain  information  about  the alleged  discrimination  such  as name,  address,  phone
number  of complainant  and  location,  date,  and  description  of the problem.  Alternative
means  of filing  complaints,  such  as  personal  interviews  or a tape  recording  of the
complaint,  will be made  available  for persons  with  disabilities  upon  request.

The  complaint  should  be submitted  by the grievant  and/or  his/her  designee  as soon  as
possible  but no later than  sixty  (60) calendar  days  after  the alleged  violation  to:

  Arturo  Cervantes
  Assistant  City Manager  / Director  of Public  Works  / ADA  Coordinator
  City of South  Gate
  South  Gate  City Hall
  8650  California  Avenue
  South  Gate,  California  90280.

Within  fifteen  (15)  calendar  days  after  receipt  of the  complaint,  Mr.  Cervantes  or his
designee  will  meet  with  the  complainant  to discuss  the  complaint  and  the  possible
resolutions.  Within  fiffeen  (15)  calendar  days  affer  that  meeting,  Mr. Cervantes  or his
designee  will  respond  in writing,  and  where  appropriate,  in a format  accessible  to the
complainant,  such  as large  print,  Braille,  or audio  tape.  The  response  will explain  the
City's  position  and offer  options  for substantive  resolution  of the complaint.

If the response  by Mr. Cervantes  or his designee  does  not satisfactorily  resolve  the issue,
the  complainant  and/or  his/her  designee  may  appeal  the  decision,  within  fiffeen  (15)
calendar  days affer the City's  delivery  of the response,  to the South  Gate  City Manager,  or
his designee.

Within  fifteen  (15)  calendar  days  affer  receipt  of the  appeal,  the  City  Manager  or his
designee  will  meet  with  the  complainant  to  discuss  the  complaint  and  possible
resolutions.  Within  fifteen  (15) calendar  days  afier  that  meeting,  the City  Manager  or his
designee  will  respond  in writing,  and,  where  appropriate,  in a format  accessible  to the
complainant,  with  a final  resolution  of the complaint.

All written  complaints  received  by Mr. Cervantes  or his designee,  all written  appeals  to
the City  Manager  or his designee,  and  all written  responses  from  these  two  officers  will
be retained  by the City for at least three  (3) years.
